New River Standard Operating Procedures
TITLE: Standard Operating Procedure Recruitment and Selection
EFFECTIVE DATE: March 1, 2024
REVISED: September 8, 2025
RESPONSIBLE OFFICE: Human Resources
RELATED POLICIES: HR: 3 Recruitment and Selection Policy; SOP: Employment Process:
Staff Performance Evaluation
PURPOSE: To establish a standardized set of procedures for recruiting and selecting a
candidate for employment.
APPLICABILITY: This procedure applies to all New River Community and Technical College
employees.
LIMITATIONS: Candidates are not allowed to begin employment until they are set up in the
payroll system of record (Oasis) and complete the hiring process (apply for the position, interview,
gain president approval, submit to post offer/pre-employment reference checks, and complete the
new hire paperwork and onboarding process. Start date is dependent on various factors.
DEFINITIONS:
Employment Request Form (ERF): a document completed by the hiring manager requesting to
fill an employment vacancy.  A job search is not started without the completion of the ERF.
• ERFs are valid for 90 days.  If a position is not filled within ninety (90) days, HR will work
with the Hiring Manager to determine if the position is still needed and/or change the
recruitment strategy.

PROCEDURE:
Step 1: Requesting to Fill a Position
A. All position requests must be within budget and pre-approved by the Chief Financial
Officer and the Divisional VP.  Any newly created positions to the budget must be pre-
approved prior to launching the Employment Request Form (ERF).

B. The Hiring Manager/Divisional VP will work with the HR Director on appropriate
compensation recommendations for the position to be posted. Compensation

recommendations are determined by scope of work, using the HEPC Master job title and
compensation matrix, reviewed for internal equity and compression and benchmarked
against other WV Community and Technical Colleges for competitive analysis. This
information is provided to the CFO and Hiring Manager for consideration before posting
the position and/or making a job offer.

C. An Employment Request Form (ERF) will be completed to request placement of
employment for an existing position, a new position, Full-time, Part-time, Work Study or
Adjunct position. All positions will be advertised on the college website, and select job
boards, such as Indeed, Glassdoor, WV Higher Ed, Zip Recruiter, etc. Any additional
advertisement must be requested by completing the Additional Advertisement
Request Form.

D. The Employment Request Form (ERF) should be completed electronically and submitted
through DocuSign for the approval signatures. All required signatures must be completed
for the request to be processed.
Signing Order:
1. Supervisor
2. Cabinet Level Supervisor if applicable
3. Director of Grants if grant funded position
4. Controller (if funding is not correct the form will be denied, and the
originator of the form will make corrections and resubmit)
5. CFO/VP Finance-Administration
6. HR Director

E. Once the approved ERF is received in Human Resources a requisition and job posting will
be created. Positions must be posted for a minimum of ten (10) days.

F. ERFs are active for 90 days only.  After 90 Days if the ERF is not filled, a re-evaluation
of the need for the position will be discussed.

Step 2: Hiring Manager and Hiring Committee Identified
A. Human Resources will work with the hiring manager to review applicants, develop the
interview questionnaire and set the interview schedule.

B. The hiring manager will select at least three individuals to serve as voting members of
the hiring committee. When requested, an HR representative can be present at either the first
or second round interviews. The members of the interview committee should have a
working knowledge and/or understanding of the duties and responsibilities of the

position to participate in the interview process. The number of interviewers will vary
depending on the position and the departments that interact with that position. (Extra
Help, Adjunct and Work Study positions do not require this step. Interviews for those
positions can be completed by the hiring manager.)

C. The Human Resources office will provide the hiring manager and/or the hiring
committee with preparation materials.  These materials include a comprehensive list of
behavior-based questions, candidate selection score sheet and a presentation reviewing
best practices for hiring.  Once the hiring committee has been selected, the hiring
manager will hold an initial meeting for the committee to provide guidance for proper
interviewing techniques, nondiscrimination and equal employment practices and
discuss the necessity for confidentiality. At the request of the hiring manager, a Human
Resources representative can conduct a review for the hiring committee. The
committee members will be reminded that notes taken during the process will become
part of the search and selection process to be retained by the Human Resources Office.
Notes should be legible.

D. The hiring manager may be part of both the first and second round of interviews or
may choose to just be part of the second round of interviews with the top
recommended candidates. The Divisional Vice President may also be included in
the second round of interviews. The hiring committee will tally the interview
score sheets.

E. The hiring manager will present the recommendation for hire to the Divisional Vice
President.

F. The Divisional Vice President (DVP) will review the recommendation and
application materials. The DVP may conduct an additional interview with the
candidate or accept the recommendation of the hiring manager.

G. The Divisional Vice President will forward the recommendation to the Office of Human
Resources.

Step 3: Candidate Approval
The Office of Human Resources will submit the recommendation and appropriate paperwork to
the President or President’s Designee.

1. The President or President’s Designee will review the final recommendation and may
choose to interview the candidate.
2. The President or President’s Designee will make the final decision on hiring the
candidate and respond to the Office of Human Resources and the hiring manager
with approval/denial.
3. Records will be maintained based on record retention guidelines.

Step 4: Offer of Employment
A. Once the candidate is approved by the President or President’s designee, the Hiring
Manager is to make the verbal offer.

B. When the verbal offer is accepted the Office of Human Resources will prepare the offer
letter, initiating the background screening, completion of new hire paperwork and the
new employee orientation process.

C. After the position is filled the Office of Human Resources will “disposition” the
candidates in the applicant tracking system.  This will trigger an email that informs
them that another candidate has been chosen, and the search is closed.

D. If the candidate is not approved or withdraws, the Office of Human Resources will
contact the hiring manager regarding the option to reconsider the other qualified
candidates or to close the search and repost the position.

Step 5: Onboarding a New Employee
• After the completion of the new employee orientation training. The hiring manager is
responsible for the effective onboarding of the new employee into the department.

• HR will provide Onboard resources to the Hiring Manager to include:
o Job description for review and signature; to be returned to HR after review and
signature
o New Hire Onboarding Plan excel template
o Onboarding Leader Guide and Checklist
o Onboarding Buddy Guide

• The Hiring Manager is responsible for developing a plan that effectively positions the
new employee for a successful integration into New River Community and Technical
College and the department team.

• Within the Introductory Period it is critical for the hiring manager to provide feedback
regarding expectations and performance.  The Hiring Manager does not need to wait until
the end of the 6-month Introductory Period to provide feedback.   HR will meet with the
Hiring Manager two weeks before the end of the Introductory Period Performance
Evaluation to determine if the individual is meeting expectations and gain the hiring
manager’s recommendation to continue or discontinue employment.
